subject: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction — follow-up and next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the intro call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the logging/redaction topics we covered: 

Summary of what we heard from FinTechCo:
- You need to ensure PII is never persisted in plain text in request/response logs.
- Retention window target: 90 days (US region).
- Headers must not contain secrets (Authorization), and trace IDs are OK if masked.
- You need clarity on what Redwood can provide for redaction (deterministic hashing vs full removal) and where logs are stored (residency).

What Redwood can provide (high level):
- Configurable logging policies per route: full logging, headers-only, no-body logging.
- Built-in redaction hooks: regex-based masking, structured field redaction, and deterministic hashing/HMAC with optional customer salt.
- Header allowlist/denylist (we strip Authorization by default) and trace-id masking options.
- Retention controls: per-customer and per-route retention TTLs; default hosted retention configurable down to 30 days (we can commit to 90 for Dedicated/Private).
- SOC 2 artifacts and a short controls summary (attached).

Attachments: redwood_socs_summary.pdf, logging_controls_matrix.xlsx (controls/options matrix).

Questions / requests for you:
1) Can you confirm whether FinTechCo requires zero logging of request bodies, or if redacted/hashed bodies are acceptable?
2) Do you require deterministic hashing (to allow matching across requests) or prefer irreversible masking?
3) Any residency requirement beyond US (e.g., specific region or on-prem)?

Next steps I propose:
- Quick security deep-dive with our security engineer (David) to walk architecture and redaction options — 45 min.
- Draft a mutual action plan (MAP) that captures retention, logging limits, and required contract language.

Availability: I can do a deep-dive Mon/Tue next week; Rishi and Neha are available as well. Please share preferred times and any additional SEC/Legal contacts we should loop in (I noted Priya Singh on your side).

Thanks,
--

Subject: Re: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PII: We require that PII (names, SSNs, full account numbers, unmasked emails) not be stored in request or response logs in plaintext. Hashing is acceptable if irreversible or salted with a customer-managed value.
- Retention: 90 days in US only for any logs that contain derived identifiers. No retention outside US.
- Request/response bodies: Prefer that request bodies are not logged in hosted environments. If Redwood can provide a configuration to disable body logging per route that would be ideal.
- Headers: Authorization and any cookie headers must be removed. We are OK with trace IDs provided the value is masked (e.g., only last 4 chars) and cannot be linked back to the full payload without a customer-secret.

Priya (cc) — looping you in for any legal/contract asks. We can share a security questionnaire; attaching a partial export here.

Can David join the deep-dive? Would like someone from your security team who can speak to KMS/key handling and log residency.

Appreciate it — request times for next week.

Alex
Director, Platform Engineering | FinTechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com

Subject: Re: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction — follow-up and next steps

Alex — thanks, that's helpful. Quick technical notes that should answer a few of your items; David can expand in the deep-dive: 

- Redaction options: 
  * No-body logging: configurable per route; hosted API can opt out of request/response body persistence.
  * Field-level redaction: structured parsers for JSON requests — you can provide a schema or we can use a best-effort extractor.
  * Deterministic hashing/HMAC: supported. For hosted customers we use tenant-scoped salts; for Dedicated/Private you can provide your own salt/KMS.
- Headers: We expose an allowlist and will strip Authorization/Cookie by default. You can also provide a header transformation policy.
- Trace IDs: We support deterministic masking (store only masked id) and an optional mapping store in Dedicated/Private deployments that can be backed by customer KMS for re-identification in emergencies.
- Retention: Per-customer TTLs; hosted defaults are conservative but we can contractually set 90d for your account and ensure logs are only kept in US regions.

I've attached logging_controls_matrix.xlsx which maps the options by deployment type (hosted / dedicated / private) and includes recommended contract language snippets for retention and access. Also attached SOC summary.

Proposed times for the security deep-dive (45 min):
- Mon Jun 22: 10:00–10:45 PT
- Tue Jun 23: 11:00–11:45 PT

If those don't work, suggest a couple times and David will join to speak on KMS, mapping storage, and redaction mechanics.

Next steps from Redwood side:
- Share a short redaction design doc (we'll send before the call).
- Draft MAP covering retention/logging limits and contract language.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Alex / Marissa — David from Redwood security team here. Happy to run the deep-dive and walk through implementation tradeoffs. A few notes ahead of the call: 

- Deterministic hashing vs irreversible masking: deterministic hashing (HMAC with salt) is useful for detecting duplicates and correlating events, but requires careful key management. For hosted deployments we can offer tenant-scoped salts stored in our KMS; for stronger guarantees we recommend Dedicated with customer-managed KMS.
- Mapping store: We avoid storing mapping tables in hosted by default. If you require re-identification for troubleshooting, we recommend a Dedicated/Private mapping store encrypted with your KMS.
- KMS: Redwood integrates with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) for Dedicated/Private. For hosted customers we provide managed KMS with strict access controls and SOC 2 controls.
- Residency: Hosted logs can be restricted to US regions; Dedicated/Private gives you full control over storage location.

I'll prepare a 1–2 page redaction design doc and bring it to the call. Please flag any architecture-specific concerns (e.g., if you run through a proxy that injects headers we should know).

David
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.com
